0.0.n: Adds a friendly introductory greeting before おはようございます.

0.1.n: Combines with ございます to make a polite morning greeting.

0.2.n: This is the stem of ござる; with ます, it makes おはよう polite.

0.3.n: Completes ございます as part of the polite greeting.

0.5.n: This is the speaker’s name, written in katakana.

0.6.n: Politely finishes the self-introduction; the speaker leaves out 私は, meaning I.

1.0.n: Introduces the reason the speaker cannot explain.

1.1.n: Describes こと as a situation like this.

1.2.n: Refers to what has happened, rather than a physical thing.

1.3.n: Marks the resulting situation with なる, meaning become.

1.4.n: Past form of なる, describing a change into the current situation.

1.5.n: Marks the end of the embedded question about why this happened.

1.6.n: Softens the admission of not knowing, rather than indicating a precise small amount.

1.7.n: Casual spoken form of 分からない, with ら becoming ん.

1.8.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone before です.

1.9.n: Makes the explanation polite despite the casual 分かんない.

1.10.n: Softly links this admission to what follows.

2.0.n: 起きたら is 起きる with a when ending; です here is a conversational politeness filler.

2.1.n: In ですね, it gently draws the listener along while the speaker pauses.

2.3.n: Although often meaning noon, お昼 here broadly refers to daytime.

2.4.n: Links the daytime period to the clock time.

2.5.n: 時 marks the hour; お昼 makes clear this is 3 p.m.

2.6.n: This is the portion of でした before the past ending た.

2.7.n: Completes でした, the polite past form of です.

3.0.n: Refers to a between-meal treat, traditionally associated with around 3 p.m.

3.1.n: Links おやつ to 時間 to form snack time.

3.2.n: Names the occasion for having a snack.

3.4.n: A noun from 目覚める, used here as a compact label for the event.

3.5.n: Casual form of という, introducing how the speaker describes the situation.

3.6.n: Here it frames the situation, rather than referring to a fictional tale.

3.7.n: The linking form of だ connects this description to the next thought.

3.9.n: Asks the reason for ending up in this situation.

3.10.n: Part of the casual phrase こんなんなって, corresponding to こんなになって.

3.11.n: Here ん belongs to the compressed spoken expression こんなんなって, rather than the explanatory んです.

3.12.n: なって is the linking form of なる; しまった adds a sense of an unfortunate or unintended result.

3.13.n: Closes the embedded why-question before 分かんない.

3.14.n: A conversational contraction of 分からない.

3.15.n: Short for の, framing the admission as an explanation.

3.16.n: Adds politeness to the explanatory phrase んです.

3.17.n: Leaves the thought open and gently leads into the possible explanation.

4.0.n: Suggests the speaker is offering a reason only after some hesitation.

4.1.n: 言う plus なら makes a conditional phrase, introducing a tentative answer.

4.3.n: Locates the sleeping event in the previous day.

4.4.n: Past form of 寝る; here it refers to starting sleep.

4.5.n: Colloquial の turns 昨日寝た into a noun-like phrase that が can mark.

4.6.n: Marks the preceding sleeping event as what the time statement describes.

4.7.n: Specifies the early-day period for the following hour.

4.8.n: Links 朝 to 5時, specifying 5 a.m.

4.9.n: 時 marks the hour; 朝 tells us it is a.m.

4.10.n: Connects the noun phrase 朝の5時 to explanatory んです.

4.11.n: Short for の, presenting the late bedtime as the reason.

4.13.n: Emphasizes information the speaker is bringing to the listener’s attention.

0.lit: Hello, good morning; I am Parker.
0.tip: おはようございます is a set polite greeting, even though the subtitle splits ございます into two pieces.

1.lit: Why it became this kind of situation, I don't really know, but…
1.tip: A question ending in か can sit inside a sentence before 分からない, meaning don't know.

2.lit: When I woke up, you know, it was three o'clock in the daytime.
2.tip: A past-form verb plus ら can mean when something happened, not just if.

3.lit: Waking at snack time is the story, and why it ended up like this, I don't know, but…
3.tip: Verb + てしまった often suggests an unintended or regrettable outcome, as with this very late wake-up.

4.lit: If pressed to say, when I went to bed yesterday was five in the morning, you see.
4.tip: 寝たんが uses ん for の to make the preceding verb phrase act like a noun.
